m1 - DECIDING VOTE, as asked: PER-CELL ELIGIBILITY, not a fixed reference weight. Argument is arithmetic.

FIXED W_ref = 3.35, scale = 3.35 / W_present:
  chartless, no sensory         3.20  ->  1.0469
  chartless, with sensory       3.35  ->  1.0000
  CELL WITH A CHART             3.85  ->  0.8701   SCALES DOWN 13%
  CELL WITH CHART + STRUCTURAL  4.35  ->  0.7701   SCALES DOWN 23%

A cell that measured MORE receives a DISCOUNT against an unmoved external floor. That is the defect
we are fixing with the sign flipped: "less evidence looks more anchorable" becomes "more evidence
looks more anchorable".

NOT MERELY A MIXED-VIEW EDGE CASE. On a corpus where charts exist throughout - the corpus M1
acquisition is meant to produce - every cell sits at 4.35 and every cost drops 23%, flipping the row
to Source. The fixed reference is calibrated to WOG's chartlessness and fails on the data we are
building toward.

THE DECISIVE FORM: NO SINGLE CONSTANT WORKS.
  4.35 inflates chartless cells 30-36% and collapses the row to External (built, measured, reverted)
  3.35 deflates chart-bearing cells 13-23% and collapses it to Source
Opposite directions, same cause: THE REFERENCE MUST DEPEND ON WHAT THE CELL COULD MEASURE, and a
constant cannot.

Per-cell yields exactly 1.0000 for every fully-measured cell whatever its eligible set, chartless or
chart-bearing. That is Law 1 generalised rather than a coincidence of this fixture.

AND IT MEETS THE CHIEF'S OWN TEST: the mean was rejected because recalibrating against WOG is
fitting the model to the fixture we validate on. W_ref = 3.35 is a constant derived from WOG's
particular lack of charts - the same objection, with more force, since the mean at least did not
pretend to be anything but a rescaling.

CAVEAT ON MY OWN CONFIDENCE: this rests on the arithmetic above, not on having imagined every view
shape. If anyone has a mixed-view case where per-cell misbehaves, I want to see it before this is
settled.
